Class Messenger

java.lang.Object
Messenger
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public class Messenger extends Object implements AutoCloseable
A UDP-based messaging module that provides a simple interface for sending and receiving messages. It supports sending messages to a specified address, receiving messages from any address. The module is designed to be used in both server and client applications. Example server sequence, for a server object that expects only to react to messages: Messenger messenger = new Messenger(null); int port = messenger.getPort(); // advertise this port to clients Messenger.Message message = messenger.receive(); System.out.println("Message from " + message.getAddr() + ": " + message.getText()); messenger.send(from, "Thanks!"); messenger.close(); Example client sequence for a client object: Messenger messenger = new Messenger(null); InetSocketAddress server = Messenger.resolveAddress(serverHost, serverPort); messenger.send(server, "hello!"); Messenger.Message message = messenger.receive(); System.out.println("Response from " + message.getAddr() + ": " + message.getText()); messenger.close(); Note: This class is thread-safe; threads that concurrently call its methods share only its member variables. Java's DatagramSocket class is thread-safe. My Log class is thread-safe. David Kotz - Fall 2026, derived from his original C module (with Claude suggesting some of the Socket details).

    • send

      public void send(InetSocketAddress to, String text) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, IOException
      send - Send a message to the given address. Overlength messages are silently truncated.
      Parameters:
      to - - the Internet address to which to send the message
      text - - the string message to send
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the address or message is null
      RuntimeException - if the socket is closed
      IOException - if an I/O error occurs while sending the message

    • resolveAddress

      public static InetSocketAddress resolveAddress(String hostname, int port) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnknownHostException
      resolveAddress - Resolve a hostname/port pair into an address suitable for send(). It throws exceptions for invalid input.
      Parameters:
      hostname - the hostname to resolve
      port - the port number as an integer
      Returns:
      an InetSocketAddress representing the resolved address
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the hostname is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the port number is not in the unreserved range (1024-65535)
      UnknownHostException - if the hostname cannot be resolved
